newsitem.title: FRANCE: Bouygues unit director in probe.
newsitem.headline: Bouygues unit director in probe.

text.p: Philippe Chalendon, managing director of a subidiary of French building giant Bouygues has been placed under investigation in a fraud probe, justice sources said on Thursday.
The sources said Chalendon was probed for misuse of corporate funds by judge Jean-Marie Charpier in Versailles outside Paris.
Police were holding in custody Bouygues chairman Martin Bouygues after releasing Patrick Le Lay, the head of private television channel TF1, overnight, the sources said.

Chalendon, managing director of the maritime branch of Bouygues Offshore, and the other two businessmen were summoned on Wednesday for questioning in the probe into false invoices involving some 40 companies in the Paris area.

The probe focuses on some five million francs ($880,000) worth of allegedly false invoices made out by Cerail consultant firm for subsidiaries of Bouygues including Saur, TF1, Bouygues Offshore and Bouygues Diversifications.
Three managers of the group have already been placed under investigation by the judge.
